FLAGS:
• FCCR has risen every quarter test from 1.7245x at the first test date to 2.1564x at June 30, 2026, roughly 80% headroom over the 1.20x minimum; continued monitoring of this trend is warranted given the amortization mechanics noted in Data quality.
  • Monthly amortization of 0.20% of beginning funded debt leaves a large balloon due at the January 2030 maturity; not a near-term concern given the current trend, but a structural feature worth tracking.
  • A working DRAFT department-to-GL mapping exists that swaps two Sales accounts' GL categories relative to the Board-approved exhibit; confirmation is open that the DRAFT version was never used for any actual monitoring or budget output.
  • Amendment/waiver/restatement history is clean: a full-text sweep of every executed document found zero amendments, waivers, or restatements since the January 2025 refinancing closing.
  • Collateral securing this facility is a specific-asset lien on receivables, equipment, and intellectual property; inventory and other current assets sit outside the lender's security package.
  • Confirmation is open on whether any named-counterparty AR/AP detail exists informally beyond the bucketed totals in the monthly aging export, to support customer or vendor concentration monitoring.
  • The identity of any parent, holding, or sponsor entity is unconfirmed; none is named in any document reviewed, consistent with this being a straight refinancing rather than a sponsor transaction.
  • Whether inventory, currently blended into the Balance Sheet's 'Inventory and Other Current Assets' line, is material enough to warrant its own reporting line is open for confirmation, particularly since it sits outside the pledged collateral.
FORWARD_STRESS: Continued EBITDA growth, not debt paydown, has driven FCCR headroom from roughly 61% to 80% over the past four test dates, since gross funded debt has declined only about 4% since the January 2025 closing; a reversal of the June gross-margin compression into a multi-month trend would test that dependence well before it tests the 1.20x minimum itself.
IS_OBSERVATIONS:
• Revenue was $13,852,035 in June 2026, up 0.25% month over month and up 6.1% year over year.

  • Net income was $1,032,520 in June 2026, down 10.1% month over month and up 22.1% year over year.
  • All four operating-expense groups (Sales, Operations, Product, Corporate) ran at or under budget both for June and year to date; the budget miss on gross profit and EBITDA traces to gross margin, not spending.
LIQUIDITY_READ:
• Cash was $13.5M at June 30, 2026 against no configured cash floor for this borrower.
  • Cash has built every month since the model's earliest period; June's movement was a build, not a burn.
OPEN_QUESTIONS: Whether June's gross-margin compression (49.8% budgeted to 45.0% actual) is a one-month cost-mix event or the start of a trend is open, since the covenant's EBITDA definition permits no add-backs and continued EBITDA growth, not debt paydown, is what has driven the FCCR trend to date. Confirmation is also open on the department-mapping discrepancy between the DRAFT and Board-approved exhibits, the identity of any parent or sponsor entity, and whether inventory warrants its own monthly reporting line.
SUMMARY_COLLATERAL: Pledged collateral, accounts receivable and net equipment, totals $33.1M against $100.5M of secured debt at June 2026, a 33.0% coverage ratio on all trackable pledged assets (18.6% on accounts receivable alone); inventory and other current assets sit outside the lien. SUMMARY_COVENANTS: The Minimum FCCR passed with wide headroom at June 30, 2026: our reconstruction reads 2.15637x against the certificate's 2.1564x, a 0.0001x gap from the certificate's rounding, and our reconstruction governs. Headroom over the 1.20x minimum has widened every quarter since the first test date; the earliest two test dates are not evaluable on the model side for lack of pre-archive history, though the certified ratio was compliant at both.
SUMMARY_LIQUIDITY: Cash was $13.5M at June 30, 2026, building every month with no covenant cash floor configured; June's cash movement was a build, funded by continued, if margin-compressed, operating cash generation. No near-term liquidity concern is indicated.
SUMMARY_OUTLOOK: The governing question is whether June's gross-margin compression is a one-month cost-mix event or the start of a trend, since Fixed Charges carry zero EBITDA add-back flexibility under the agreement and continued EBITDA growth, not debt paydown, is what has driven the FCCR trend to date, as gross funded debt has fallen only about 4% since closing. Open asks include confirming the department-mapping discrepancy was never used operationally, the identity of any parent or sponsor entity, and whether inventory warrants its own reporting line.

_contract.deep_links: a reference to another section is written Covenant detail ↗ — same markup, any section id below

flags_must_name.rule: the FLAGS box covers every open item; the gate looks for each item's identifying token (or its dollar amount) in your prose

_contract.how: Fill every key; values are HTML. Leave a box "" when the month gives it nothing, and say so in your report. Keys opening with "_" (this note) are ignored by the renderer.

keyed_boxes.CAPSTRUCTURE_NOTES: per row id: the instrument's pricing or terms in one clause
keyed_boxes.COVENANT_DELTAS: per covenant id: one clause on WHY the certified figure and ours differ — the component that carries the gap, named. Our reconstruction governs; do not write that the borrower's basis governs, whichever way the gap runs
keyed_boxes.DOCUMENT_NOTES: per document id: what the document is and what it settles, one sentence

_contract.language: lead with the fact and its figure; the banned words and patterns are in references/report-structure.md under the language contract

  • …

summary_blocks.SUMMARY_COLLATERAL: pledged components and their total, coverage against funded debt, and the prior-year or plan comparison where one is on file
summary_blocks.SUMMARY_COVENANTS: one sentence when everything passes with room; otherwise the failing or governing leg, the certified-vs-model gap, and the nearest tight test with what clearing it takes
summary_blocks.SUMMARY_LIQUIDITY: period-end cash against the floor, where the cash came from (earned, borrowed, working capital), months of runway when burning, and the expected direction with its basis
summary_blocks.SUMMARY_OUTLOOK: the forward indicators on file (backlog, order book, seasonality), the governing question for the credit, and the open asks — never a concern manufactured to fill the space
summary_blocks.SUMMARY_UPDATE: revenue and EBITDA vs Budget and prior year — the period first, the cumulative line second — then the driver: which segment or brand moved, mix or margin, at the finest level the package reports
summary_blocks.bad_news: a miss, a breach or a stretch is written in its home block with the same syntax as a beat — there is no separate red-flags list, and a fired concern must not be left out of its block
summary_blocks.cadence: the renderer titles the first block from the period: a March/June/September/December period reads 'Quarterly update' and its prose covers the quarter and the year so far; any other month reads 'Monthly update' and covers the month and the year so far
summary_blocks.numbers: round to $X.XM / $XXXK in these five blocks; full precision lives in the tables, where every figure is click-traceable
summary_blocks.what: the executive summary is the analyst's one-pager for the deal team: five labelled prose blocks, each 2-5 sentences, written the way a portfolio review reads — the figure, its comparator (vs Budget, vs prior year), then the driver. The template owns the labels; write only the prose.
